title: US provider contraction is widespread across the comparison set, but not universal
source_unit: IMF Financial Access Survey annual provider-reported country series; selected economy comparison
geography: United States, Canada, Germany, United Kingdom, China, India, Brazil, South Africa, and Mexico

denominator.unit: country provider count; no common customer or population denominator

commercial_bank_count_2020.value: USA 4,344; CAN 79; DEU 257; GBR 313; CHN 192; IND 151; BRA 121; ZAF 34; MEX 50

commercial_bank_count_2024.value: USA 3,912; CAN 75; DEU 234; GBR 273; CHN 183; IND 141; BRA 152; ZAF 30; MEX 51

change_2020_to_2024.unit: percent change in reported provider count

observations.method: Same IMF FAS COMBANK series and 2020/2024 endpoints for nine selected economies; changes calculated from returned country values.
observations.uncertainty: Provider counts are administrative/reporting measures. Country definitions, consolidation, licensing, reporting coverage, and institutional classification differ; counts are not market shares, branch access, competition, or customer welfare.
observations.subgroup: Country/provider-level comparison; no customer, income, geographic, gender, or rurality subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: Brazil and Mexico show increases in reported commercial-bank counts while most selected economies decline, demonstrating that the US pattern is not universal. An increase can still coexist with concentration, weak access, or poor terms.

observations.period: 2020–2024; commercial-bank branch density across selected economies

denominator.unit: commercial-bank branches per 100,000 adults; country-specific adult denominator

branch_density_2020.unit: branches per 100,000 adults; GBR not available in returned series

branch_density_2024.unit: branches per 100,000 adults; GBR not available in returned series

density_change_2020_to_2024.unit: percent change in adult-normalized branch density

observations.method: Same IMF FAS FA26N series selected with UNIT=NUM and adult-normalized PHTADLT_NUM transformation; countries with no returned series are retained as unavailable, not zero.
observations.uncertainty: Density does not measure travel, branch hours, cash availability, digital substitution, service quality, or human remedy. Country reporting and adult-population denominators may differ.
observations.subgroup: Country/provider-level comparison; no place or customer subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: China and India show near-flat density in this slice while Brazil, Germany, and the US decline; this weakens a single global branch-contraction narrative but does not identify why routes differ.

denominator.unit: country-specific IMF FAS indicator universe; balance ratios use GDP, not households

household_deposit_ratio_change.value: USA -23.6%; DEU +0.5%; GBR -11.4%; IND -9.7%; ZAF +1.2%; other selected economies unavailable in returned series
household_deposit_ratio_change.unit: percent change in household commercial-bank deposits as percent of GDP

household_loan_ratio_change.value: USA -15.6%; DEU -12.8%; GBR -18.4%; IND +11.1%; ZAF -5.2%; MEX +12.2%; BRA 2020 unavailable and 2024 27.65%; other selected economies unavailable
household_loan_ratio_change.unit: percent change in household commercial-bank loans as percent of GDP where both endpoints exist

observations.method: Same OUTD_COMBANK_S14 and OUTL_COMBANK_S14 series where both country-year endpoints were returned; unavailable country-year cells are not imputed.
observations.uncertainty: Ratios to GDP combine financial balances and macro denominators and are not comparable to household liquidity, debt burden, approval, affordability, or welfare without additional data.
observations.subgroup: Commercial-bank household-sector balance aggregates; no individual or household subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: India's loan ratio rises while its bank count falls and branch density is stable; South Africa's deposit ratio is nearly stable while its bank and branch counts decline. This shows why no single provider metric can stand for access or room.

denominator.unit: separate provider aggregates and adult-survey aggregates; no common person or account denominator

cross_country_counterexample.value: India: commercial-bank count -6.6%, branch density +0.5%, household loan ratio +11.1%
cross_country_counterexample.unit: separate IMF FAS provider and balance indicators

observations.method: Descriptive alignment of the IMF FAS nine-country provider comparison with the World Bank Findex US account-ownership series; no pooled or causal estimate.
observations.uncertainty: Sources differ in unit, timing, collection design, definitions, missingness, and denominator. The comparison identifies measurement divergence and counterexamples, not a mechanism.
observations.subgroup: US-centered comparison with selected economies; no aligned household or customer subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital channels, nonbanks, mergers, policy, macro growth, and reporting changes may explain different provider/user movements. Findex account ownership cannot be used as a direct outcome of branch contraction.

related_sources.claim: IMF FAS is the provider-side annual financial-access source and documents the indicator family and methodology context.
World Bank Findex supplies adult-reported demand-side account and connectivity measures for comparison.

boundary: The selected-country comparison shows that US provider contraction is widespread but not universal: Brazil and Mexico report increases in commercial-bank counts, China and India show near-flat branch density, and balance ratios move differently across countries. The result identifies heterogeneous institutional paths, not a global digital-finance mechanism or a household welfare effect. Missing country indicators remain missing, and provider aggregates are not silently converted into user outcomes.
